title: Note on the trace of random walks on pseudorandom graphs
summary: We study the graph-theoretic properties of the trace of random walks on pseudorandom graphs. We show that for any $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a constant $C$ such that the cover time of an $(n,d,λ)$-graph $G$ with $d/λ\ge C$ is at most $(1+\varepsilon)n\log n$, meaning the expected number of steps needed to reach all vertices at least once is at most $(1+\varepsilon)n\log n$ regardless of the starting vertex. Furthermore, we prove that with high probability, the trace of a random walk of length $(1+\varepsilon)n\log n$ on $G$ is Hamiltonian, regardless of the starting vertex. These results…
